slides: Your muscles aren’t the only thing that get stronger.
Each rep trains your nervous system to fire faster.
Consistent load increases motor‑unit recruitment.
That translates to more power before the next workout.
Strength is as much brain as brawn.
Want a new habit? Piggyback on an existing cue.
Your coffee routine already triggers a morning window.
Add a 2‑minute stretch right after the first sip.
The cue is automatic, the new action rides its momentum.
Stacked habits stick without willpower battles.
Sleep is the only workout you can’t skip and still see gains.
During deep REM, growth hormone floods your bloodstream.
It repairs fibers, clears metabolic waste, and resets hormones.
Eight hours is the sweet spot; less is a training deficit.
Prioritize rest like a lift – the results speak.
Your daily decisions should echo your core values.
Write down the three principles that define you.
Before acting, ask: Does this align with them?
If the answer is no, reframe or reject the choice.
Alignment turns intent into effortless execution.
